### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, A01 was not observed in any of the 200 traces; in the later window it runs in about 16 in 100 traces (31 of 200), averages roughly 0.29 occurrences per trace, and repeats within the same trace in about 8 in 100 traces. [OCC001]
- In the later window, A01 sits around two-thirds of the way through the trace (median relative position about 0.70, quartiles roughly 0.51–0.88). Its outgoing transitions lead to A09 in about 54 in 100 and to A10 in about 46 in 100 of the observed transitions; A08, which never led to A01 before, now transitions to A01 in about 8 in 100 of its outgoing transitions, while its shares towards A11–A14 each shrink slightly. [POS001, DIR001, DIR005]
- In the earlier window, A01 never co-occurred with any other tracked activity; in the later window it co-occurs with A02, A04, A05, A08, A10 and A15 in essentially all of its traces (co-occurrence about 0.13–0.16 versus 0 before), usually interleaved with A08 and mostly after A02 and A04. Traces containing A08 without A01 fell from about 24 in 100 to about 8 in 100. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL006, REL011]
- The trio A02/A04/A05 ran in about 47 in 100 traces before and about 54 in 100 after, with their mutual order and outgoing transition shares essentially unchanged; this is a modest shift. [OCC002, OCC004, REL012, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004]
- Several activities became less frequent in the later window: A07 participation fell from about 18 to 10 in 100 traces; A12 averaged 0.49 versus 0.32 occurrences per trace with an earlier median position (about 0.64 versus 0.46); A13 fell from 0.28 to 0.18 occurrences per trace with a later median position (about 0.68 versus 0.79); A14 fell from 0.23 to 0.11 occurrences per trace. [OCC007, OCC012, POS009, OCC013, POS010, OCC014]
- A few step-gap distributions shifted (for example, the share of A10→A11 pairs three steps apart rose from about 0.18 to 0.65, and A09→A12 two-step gaps from about 0.30 to 0.56), but each rests on roughly 9–14 observations per window. [LAG049, LAG043]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that A01 was introduced into the process in the later window: an activity not observed before now executes in about 16 in 100 traces, typically after A08 (and after the A02/A04 block), around two-thirds of the way through the trace, and is followed by A09 or A10. This rests on direct, mutually consistent observations from four indicator families — occurrence rising from zero, the new edges A08→A01 and A01→A09/A10, a new position distribution, and co-occurrence with the main activities rising from none to near-complete overlap — and every item in this A01 cluster shows a difference larger than in about 97 in 100 random re-splits of the pooled data. [OCC001, DIR001, DIR005, POS001, REL001, REL004, REL006]

The main limitation is that zero participation in the earlier window strictly shows only that A01 was not observed there: with 200 traces per window, a pre-existing but rarer A01 missed by sampling cannot be fully excluded, and the evidence cannot indicate why A01 appears. [OCC001]

Other differences: the higher participation of A02/A04/A05 (about 47 to 54 in 100 traces), the lower participation of A07 and the lower occurrence with shifted positions of A12, A13 and A14, and the small step-gap shifts listed above are not explained by the A01 hypothesis; the step-gap shifts in particular rest on very few observations. [OCC002, OCC007, OCC012, OCC013, OCC014, LAG049, LAG043]
